st: Lay the eggplant slices on trays and sprinkle with [[1 tsp]] salt. Let sit 20 minutes, then pat dry with paper towels.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Brush the slices with [[0.5 cup]] olive oil in total and roast on lined trays for 25 minutes, flipping once, until golden. Lower the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Brown the lamb in a large pan over medium-high heat for 8 minutes, breaking it up. Add the onion and garlic and cook 5 minutes.
Add the wine (or water), tomatoes, cinnamon, oregano, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Simmer for 20 minutes until thick.
Make the bechamel: melt the butter in a pot, whisk in the flour and cook 2 minutes. Slowly whisk in the milk and cook, stirring, about 8 minutes until thick.
Off the heat, whisk in the nutmeg, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and the cheese. Let cool 5 minutes, then whisk in the egg yolks.
In a 9x13 inch dish, layer half the eggplant, all the meat sauce, then the remaining eggplant.
Pour the bechamel over the top and smooth it out.
Bake for 40 minutes until the top is golden and bubbling.
Rest for 20 minutes before cutting so the layers set.
Mix the lemon juice, [[0.25 cup]] olive oil, oregano, garlic, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and the pepper in a bowl.
Add the pork, toss well, cover and marinate in the fridge for at least 2 hours.
If using wooden skewers, soak 8 of them in water for 30 minutes. Thread the pork onto the skewers.
Heat a grill or cast-iron pan over medium-high heat and oil it lightly.
Cook the skewers for 10 to 12 minutes, turning every few minutes, until browned and the pork reaches 145°F (63°C).
Warm the pita on the grill for 30 seconds per side.
Slide the meat off the skewers into the pita with tomato, onion and tzatziki, and roll up.
Mix the olive oil, half the garlic, oregano, paprika, cumin, lemon juice, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Coat the pork slices and marinate for at least 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the potato fries with the vegetable oil and a pinch of salt, and spread on a tray.
Roast the potatoes for 30 minutes, turning once, until crisp and golden.
Stir the yogurt with the remaining garlic and a pinch of salt for a quick sauce.
Heat a large skillet over high heat. Cook the pork in batches for 3 to 4 minutes per batch until browned at the edges and cooked through to 145°F (63°C).
Warm the pita in a dry pan or the oven.
Fill each pita with pork, tomato, onion, a few fries and the yogurt sauce, then fold and serve.

ing: washed and chopped, or 20 oz frozen, thawed and squeezed dry
st: Heat [[2 tbsp]] olive oil in a large pan and cook the onion and green onions for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the fresh spinach in handfuls and cook until wilted, about 4 minutes. Transfer to a colander and press out as much liquid as you can, then let cool.
In a big bowl, mix the spinach, feta, eggs, dill, nutmeg, pepper and salt.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Brush a 9x13 inch pan with olive oil.
Lay a sheet of phyllo in the pan and brush with olive oil. Repeat until you have 10 layers, keeping the unused sheets under a damp towel.
Spread the spinach filling over the layers evenly.
Top with 10 more oiled phyllo sheets, brushing each. Brush the top with the remaining oil and score the top layers into squares.
Bake for 45 minutes until deep golden and crisp.
Cool 15 minutes, then cut along the scored lines.
Cut the tomatoes into wedges and put them in a wide bowl.
Add the cucumber, red onion, olives and bell pepper rings if using.
Sprinkle with [[0.5 tsp]] salt and the vinegar, then drizzle with half of the [[0.25 cup]] olive oil. Toss gently.
Place the slab of feta on top.
Sprinkle the feta with the oregano and drizzle with the remaining olive oil.
Serve right away with crusty bread to mop up the juices.
Boil the pasta in well-salted water for 2 minutes less than the package says. Drain, toss with [[2 tbsp]] of the butter and half the eggs.
Heat the olive oil in a large pan. Cook the onion for 5 minutes, then add the garlic and beef. Brown the beef well for 8 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, crushed tomatoes, cinnamon, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Simmer for 20 minutes until thick.
Make the bechamel: melt [[4 tbsp]] butter in a pot, whisk in the flour and cook for 2 minutes. Slowly whisk in the milk and cook about 8 minutes until thick.
Off the heat, stir in [[0.5 cup]] cheese, the nutmeg, [[1 tsp]] salt and the remaining beaten egg.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Spread half the pasta in a 9x13 inch dish, then all the meat sauce, then the rest of the pasta.
Pour the bechamel over the top and sprinkle with the remaining [[0.5 cup]] cheese.
Bake for 40 minutes until the top is golden. Rest 15 minutes before cutting.
Rinse the grape leaves in warm water and trim off any hard stems. Set aside a few torn leaves.
Heat [[0.25 cup]] olive oil in a pan and cook the onion and green onions for 5 minutes. Add the rice and stir 2 minutes.
Off the heat, mix in the dill, mint, juice of 1 lemon, salt and pepper. Let cool.
Place a leaf shiny side down, with the stem end toward you. Put a heaping teaspoon of filling near the stem end.
Fold in the sides, then roll up tightly like a small cigar. Repeat with all leaves.
Line a heavy pot with the torn leaves. Pack the rolls seam side down in tight layers.
Pour over [[2 cups]] hot water, the remaining lemon juice and [[0.25 cup]] olive oil. Set a plate on top to keep them from unrolling.
Cover and simmer on low for 45 minutes until the rice is tender.
Cool in the pot. Serve at room temperature or chilled with lemon.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Scoop the pulp out of the tomatoes and chop it, saving the juices. Hollow out the peppers.
Heat [[0.25 cup]] olive oil in a pan and cook the onion for 5 minutes, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomato pulp and cook 8 minutes. Stir in the rice, tomato paste, sugar, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Cook 2 minutes.
Off the heat, stir in the parsley and mint.
Sprinkle the inside of the tomatoes and peppers with a pinch of salt. Fill them about three-quarters full, since the rice will swell.
Stand them upright in a baking dish, snug together, with the potato wedges in the gaps. Put the tops back on.
Pour [[0.5 cup]] water around them and drizzle with the remaining [[0.25 cup]] olive oil and [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Bake for 60 to 70 minutes, basting once, until the rice is tender and the edges brown.
Rest 15 minutes and serve warm or at room temperature.
Put the chicken, onion, carrot, celery and [[8 cups]] water in a pot. Bring to a boil, skim off any foam, then simmer for 30 minutes until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Lift out the chicken and strain the broth back into the pot. Discard the vegetables.
Season the broth with [[1.5 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Add the rice and simmer for 15 minutes until tender.
Shred the chicken, discarding the skin and bones.
Whisk the eggs in a bowl until frothy, then whisk in the lemon juice.
Slowly ladle about [[1 cup]] of hot broth into the eggs, whisking constantly so they do not scramble.
Turn the heat to low. Stir the egg mixture into the pot and add the chicken. Heat gently for 3 minutes without boiling.
Taste, add salt or lemon, sprinkle with dill, and serve right away.
Drain the soaked beans and put them in a large pot with fresh water to cover. Boil for 10 minutes, then drain and rinse.
In the clean pot, heat [[0.33 cup]] olive oil over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrots and celery for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic and tomato paste and stir for 1 minute.
Add the beans, tomatoes, bay leaves, oregano and [[8 cups]] fresh water. Bring to a boil.
Lower the heat, partly cover and simmer for 1 hour 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until the beans are very soft.
Add [[2 tsp]] salt and the pepper and simmer 10 minutes more, until the soup is thick.
Discard the bay leaves. Serve topped with parsley and a drizzle of olive oil.
Grate the cucumber on a box grater and sprinkle with a pinch of the salt. Let it sit for 5 minutes.
Squeeze the cucumber hard in a clean towel to remove as much water as you can.
Put the yogurt in a bowl and stir in the cucumber.
Add the garlic, [[2 tbsp]] olive oil, dill and [[1 tbsp]] lemon juice.
Season with the remaining salt and the pepper and stir well.
Chill for at least 1 hour so the flavors blend, then serve with a drizzle of olive oil.
Make the syrup: boil [[1 cup]] sugar, [[1 cup]] water, the honey and lemon juice for 10 minutes. Cool completely.
Mix the walnuts with [[0.25 cup]] sugar, the cinnamon and cloves.
Heat the oven to 325°F (165°C). Brush a 9x13 inch pan with melted butter.
Lay a phyllo sheet in the pan, brush with butter, and repeat until you have 8 sheets.
Spread a third of the nut mix, then add 3 buttered sheets. Repeat twice more, finishing with the remaining nuts.
Add the last 5 buttered sheets on top and brush with all the remaining butter.
Cut into diamonds or squares with a sharp knife before baking, all the way through.
Bake for 50 minutes until deep golden.
Pour the cooled syrup evenly over the hot baklava right when it comes out.
Let it soak for at least 4 hours before serving.
Stir the yeast and sugar into the warm water. Let sit for 5 minutes until foamy.
Whisk the flour and salt in a large bowl. Pour in the yeast water and mix into a very soft, sticky batter.
Cover and let rise in a warm spot for 1 hour until doubled and bubbly.
Warm the honey with [[2 tbsp]] water and the lemon juice in a small pot, then keep it warm.
Heat [[4 cups]] oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Wet a spoon, scoop a walnut-sized blob of batter, and push it into the oil with another spoon. Fry 6 at a time.
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until deep golden and puffed. Drain on paper towels.
Pile onto a plate, drizzle with the warm honey and sprinkle with cinnamon and walnuts. Serve at once.
